source: Canadian Space Agency (CSA), 'Growing healthy food in space and in remote areas'
type: facts written from a CSA web page, not live data
note: These are facts for game cards, not measurements. Game values for food (how much a crop grows, how fast food runs out) are made up by our team and must be labelled as game values.

facts.headline: Fresh food deliveries
facts.fact: Astronauts on the International Space Station get shipments of fresh food every few months.
facts.gameLink: Resupply: the Moon base can't count on deliveries

facts.headline: Too far for deliveries
facts.fact: On missions to the Moon or Mars, resupply trips will be less frequent or even impossible, so astronauts will need to grow their own food.
facts.gameLink: Why the outpost needs a garden

facts.headline: Space food rules
facts.fact: Space food has to be compact and lightweight, and it also has to be nutritious and tasty.
facts.gameLink: Food has a cost: weight and space

facts.headline: Made to last
facts.fact: Food is chosen and packaged to last for the whole length of a mission.
facts.gameLink: Food stock that lasts the mission

facts.headline: How many calories?
facts.fact: Astronaut menus have between 1,900 and 3,200 calories a day, depending on what each crew member needs.

facts.headline: Space food helps Earth
facts.fact: Learning to grow food in harsh places like space can also help remote communities on Earth, such as northern Canada, get fresh food.
